summary: Can the string become a palindrome by deleting at most one character?
mainInsight: Use two pointers from both ends. On the first mismatch, the answer is true iff the remaining substring is a palindrome after skipping either the left or the right character. Only one deletion is allowed, so only the first mismatch needs both branches.

approaches.name: Two pointers with one skip
approaches.summary: On mismatch check s[l+1..r] and s[l..r-1].

commonMistakes: Not re-checking the rest of the substring

promptVariants: What do you do at the first mismatch?
How is the single deletion handled?
options: Test whether skipping the left character or the right character leaves a palindrome
Delete both of the mismatching characters and continue
Return false at once, since it is not a palindrome
Restart the scan from the middle of the whole string
cards.answer: Test whether skipping the left character or the right character leaves a palindrome
cards.explanation: Either mismatching character may be the one to remove.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Restart the scan from the middle of the: The mismatch location is what matters.

promptVariants: Why is it enough to branch only at the first mismatch?
cards.answer: Only one deletion is allowed. Before the first mismatch the ends already match, so the deletion must involve one of the two mismatching characters; after skipping one, the rest must match exactly, with no further deletions.
keyPoints: Delete one of the two mismatching characters

cards.explanation: Two passes at most, each linear.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___
Is 'madame' a valid answer with one deletion?
options: Yes: delete the final 'e' to get 'madam'
Yes, but only by deleting the first 'm'
cards.answer: Yes: delete the final 'e' to get 'madam'
cards.explanation: At the first mismatch (m vs e), skipping the right character leaves 'madam', a palindrome.

incorrectOptionExplanations.No: 'madame' has two mismatched pairs: Only the outer pair mismatches; the inner letters match.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Yes, but only by deleting the first 'm': Deleting the first 'm' leaves 'adame', which is not a palindrome.
incorrectOptionExplanations.No: palindromes need odd length: Even-length strings can become palindromes too.
